claim_scope: Sizing the population a bounded PHP transfer replay needs. One whole-repository scan, detection only, no comparison.
why: The earlier bounded attempt failed for a reason no budget increase could fix: 25 regions of 4,461 is 0.6% of the population and the declared target was never asked about. A three-case replay costs hours, so the budget is established with one scan first.
the_target_itself: `$wpdb->get_var("SELECT id FROM $wpdb->pmpro_membership_orders WHERE code = '" . $code . "' LIMIT 1")`. A value concatenated into SQL with no prepare, which is the declared M3 target for PHP and is detected here for the first time.
what_changed_to_make_it_reachable: Nothing about detection. The population became affordable: tier-zero pruning scoped to its partition (7.3), batches budgeted by the sink work they imply (7.7), a per-query timeout no longer cancelling the scan, and a reserve kept for arbitration. Before those, this population completed zero questions at any budget tried.
cost_implied_for_the_replay: One whole-repository scan at this budget costs 2,950 s. A push transaction is two scans plus discovery and preparation, so a case is roughly 6,600 s and the three declared comparisons roughly five and a half hours. That is the price of the population that contains the target.
limits: Detection only. This scan makes no comparison and establishes no novelty, which is what the replay is for.
271 of 406 questions completed, so the population is examined but not exhausted.
PMPro is a development subject and qualifies nothing.
